result.rationale: The diff adds `add_members` which does `usernames.split(",").each { ... User.find_by_username(username) ... group.add(user) }` with no strip and no length cap. Unlike `create`, which explicitly strips ('params[:name] || '').strip), usernames are used raw, so whitespace around names will silently fail to match, and an arbitrarily large comma-separated list triggers serial per-user queries. Both are admin-authenticated endpoints, so this is a substantive robustness/efficiency concern about newly added nontrivial logic rather than a clear correctness defect, and no test covers unstripped or overs

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff introduces `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end` with no `strip`/normalization and no cap. This means inputs like "bob, alice" will attempt to look up " alice" (leading space) and fail to add intended users, and a very long comma-separated list will trigger many sequential `find_by_username` calls and adds in one request.
